alternative: Compose the payload and the dependent part as ordinary fields and build them in a constructor function in an order that satisfies the dependency (let buf = ...; let stream = Stream::new(buf); FileStream { buf, stream }), sharing with Rc/Arc when both sides need the same value. Where a field would have to refer to another field of the same value, the owner must live outside the struct or a self-referential-struct crate must package it. Rust has no inheritance, so there is no base subobject to relocate.
idiom_name: plain fields built in a constructor function (no inheritance, no base list to order)
implementation_notes: Rust has no inheritance: the language reference is blunt that there is no way to define a struct that inherits another struct's fields and method implementations (barring macros), with shared behaviour arriving through trait default methods and generics instead. There is consequently no base subobject, no base-specifier list and no base-before-member rule to satisfy, so the classic structure cannot be written and is not needed - what replaces it is the constructor function: compute the payload into a local, then build the struct with both the payload and the dependent sub-struct, in whatever order the code states. The one part Rust cannot serve is identity: a struct cannot hold a reference to another field of itself (that is a self-referential type), so when the 'base' must be bound to the object's own member the payload has to be shared through an owner outside the struct (Rc/Arc), an index, or a self-referential-struct crate.
pitfalls: A struct whose field must point at another field of the same value is self-referential and does not compile; sharing through Rc/Arc, an index, or a dedicated crate (self_cell, ouroboros) is the only way, because there is no stable address for a base subobject to hold.

Clone-based workarounds silently copy the payload where the C++ idiom shares one instance: for a buffer the copy changes both the memory behaviour and the semantics, and it is easy to introduce by accident when the borrow checker rejects the direct version.

Trait default methods are not inheritance of state - a trait cannot carry the payload, and a type that wants both the shared behaviour and the data has to declare the fields itself, which is exactly the composition answer.
